item.title: 11 Years Later, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Finally Nails Akira Toriyama's Original Vision
item.description: I’ll be the first to admit I wasn’t particularly excited about Dragon Ball Super: Beerus . When the remake of Dragon Ball Super was first announced, I struggled to see the point of revisiting a story that had already been told once in Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods and then again in the original 2015 television run. Sure, the promise of refreshed animation was exciting, but it didn’t feel like that was enough to justify starting from scratch for a third time, especially when major manga milestones like the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc and Moro have yet to receive their due on-screen.

item.title: America's Dominance in The Game Awards Is Officially Over
item.description: This week, as well as confirming details such as the eligibility cutoff date (yes, as predicted, Grand Theft Auto 6 sneaks in just under the wire ), The Game Awards has revealed the composition of the 2026 jury . And the biggest change is the dramatically reduced presence of U.S. media.

item.title: 13 Years Ago, Rockstar Suffered a Leak Worse Than GTA 6
item.description: What could possibly be worse than footage of the world's most anticipated video game leaking onto the internet early , in an unfinished state? Easy. A game with a similar cultural footprint becoming playable ahead of its release. It seems unthinkable now in the age of Denuvo, but this exact nightmare scenario happened for Rockstar ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto 5 .

item.title: Before Dark Souls, FromSoftware’s Forgotten PS1 Horror Game Was a Haunting Exercise in Empathy
item.description: To trace FromSoftware’s history is to uncover a lineage written in cold sweat. While the studio is celebrated today for unforgiving action RPGs like Dark Souls and Elden Ring , its DNA is deeply rooted in games that feel born of a fever dream. FromSoft’s darker legacy lives in games like Kuon , a masterclass in Japanese folklore and survival horror, and Shadow Tower , a claustrophobic dungeon crawler that turns every dark alcove into a deadly trap. Even Eternal Ring — not to be confused with its blockbuster sibling Elden Ring — radiates that signature, unsettling aura that makes exploring FromSoftware’s later worlds so intoxicating.

item.title: The 10 Best Horror Books of All Time According to Goodreads, Ranked
item.description: Horror is an extremely broad genre, spanning supernatural tales and stories of mundane but twisted killers. It can be tinged with romance, fused with sci-fi , or focused on mystery. Everyone has their own fears, so choosing the most effective horror novels is a daunting task. We’ve turned to the wisdom of the crowd by consulting Goodreads, whose millions of members have rated the books that keep them up at night, and it turns out they really like Stephen King. Here’s a ranked list of the top 10 books they chose and why you should read them this spooky season.

item.title: Stephen King and Stanley Kubrick's Near-Perfect Psychological Thriller Is Officially Back on Streaming
item.description: Stephen King is a vocal guy. The Master of Horror has published over 65 novels and novellas, countless short stories, and five nonfiction books since the mid-’70s. The hype that surrounds him is well deserved. King is the kind of writer who appeals to everyone, whether you’re a genre enthusiast or a literary snob. His work has been adapted into TV shows and films, and he’s never afraid to voice his complaints and praise in equal measure. But there’s one adaptational grudge that towers above all.

item.title: 60 Years Ago, the Best Charlie Brown Quote Was So Perfect It Made It Into the Movie
item.description: Lucy’s quote, “Happiness is a warm puppy,” is another great one that touches on life’s simple joys on a really deep level. But to determine the best quote ever uttered by Charlie Brown, I didn't want accidental brilliance, I wanted something that he understands as much as the audience does. Something where he’s telling you who he is with complete self awareness. I wanted the character's philosophy on life. To me, that’s the difference between a brilliant Charlie Brown quote and brilliant Charles Schulz quote, if that makes sense.

item.title: 42 Years Later, the Definitive Sci-Fi Action Thriller is Free to Watch on YouTube
item.description: Terminator 2: Judgment Day is the rare sequel where just about everybody likes it better than the original. That’s for good reason. The 1991 sci-fi action thriller redefined the blockbuster with a relentlessly exciting story, mind-blowing special effects, and the superstar presence of Arnold Schwarzenegger. The movie is so good it often outshines its predecessor, which also redefined the action thriller in the 1980s and is still exhilarating to watch for an entirely different reason than its sequel.
